open_points.subject: artifact vocabulary
open_points.text: “The artifact types Registry accepts, and the one owner service of each, are declared in the specification” but no accepted type-to-owner mapping is declared in this text.
open_points.question: What is the complete artifact-type vocabulary, and which service owns each type?
options: Declare the complete mapping in State 0
Name another authoritative specification containing the mapping
Treat only PresuPro estimates and Cabinet Kernel pointers as declared, with exact type names still to be supplied
open_points.default_guess: Accept an `estimate` type owned by PresuPro and require exact Cabinet Kernel types before implementing them.

open_points.subject: customer erasure survivors
open_points.text: “the Customer keeps only its identity and the fact that it was erased” conflicts with “name, phone, e-mail and language are gone,” which does not say that kind, tax id, legal name, restriction state or relationship-end date are removed.
open_points.question: Exactly which Customer facts survive erasure, especially fiscal data, kind, restriction state and relationship-end date?
options: Keep only `customer_ref` and the erased fact
Erase contact data only and retain fiscal and lifecycle facts
Keep identity plus a specified non-personal subset
open_points.default_guess: Keep only `customer_ref` and the erased fact, removing all other Customer values and states.

open_points.subject: customer ordinary-name disclosure
open_points.text: “Other services keep no customer record and no copy of these values; they read them by `customer_ref` or project id when they use them” includes the customer’s name, but the only service read, “read a customer’s billing data,” expressly returns “never its contact data, the ordinary name included.”
open_points.question: May any service read a customer’s ordinary name, and if so through which operation and under what authorization; if not, how do services that previously used it stop keeping a copy?
options: The ordinary name remains owner-only
Add a dedicated authorized service read
Services use legal name instead and never receive ordinary name
open_points.default_guess: Keep the ordinary name owner-only and require services needing a document name to use the legal name returned by the billing read.

open_points.subject: Client Portal offline projection
open_points.text: “Client Portal’s offline projection” and “it holds only what the customer’s own cabinet shows, never a tax id” do not name the values it may store, while “The customer’s contact data reaches the owner alone.”
open_points.question: Which exact Registry values may Client Portal’s offline projection retain, and may it contain the customer’s name or other contact data, the project display name, address or object characteristics?
options: Identity fields only
Identity plus specified project personal-data fields
Any values shown in the cabinet except tax id
No customer contact data but a declared subset of project personal data
open_points.default_guess: Allow only a separately enumerated projection containing identity and the minimum project fields published to that customer, with no customer contact or fiscal data.

open_points.subject: test-instance imports
open_points.text: “nothing moves between an instance and production except by an explicit import” conflicts with “The only source is the Registry on the VPS, imported once” and “The local instance and the test rig are not sources.”
open_points.question: Can a test instance ever be explicitly imported into production after the one VPS migration, or is production import permanently limited to that VPS migration?
options: Only the one VPS migration is permitted
Future explicit imports from test instances are permitted
A different future operation may promote test data
open_points.default_guess: Limit import permanently to the one VPS migration; test instances can never be production sources.

open_points.subject: external AI provider boundary
open_points.text: “Agent — any language-model agent acting for the owner” and “The rule closes the path ... through Cabinet Kernel and so the agent’s AI provider” do not define the AI provider as an actor or state which non-personal disclosure classes and values may cross that boundary.
open_points.question: Is the external AI provider a separate recipient, and which Registry-derived values or disclosure classes may be sent to it through the agent?
options: Treat the provider as part of the Agent actor with the same permissions
Name it as a separate processor allowed `business_confidential` but never `personal_data`
Permit only a narrower declared projection
No external provider receives Registry-derived values
open_points.default_guess: Treat the provider as a separate external recipient allowed the agent projection under `business_confidential`, never `personal_data`.

open_points.subject: end-to-end agent personal-data guarantee
open_points.text: The Agent actor says it “never receives a value Registry holds as `personal_data`,” while R0-74 says “What other services cleared for `personal_data` pass on to Kernel is bounded by their own contracts, not here.”
open_points.question: Is the no-personal-data promise an end-to-end platform guarantee covering Cabinet and other services, or only a guarantee about Registry’s direct outputs to Kernel?
options: End-to-end guarantee enforced by every service contract
Registry-direct-output guarantee only
End-to-end guarantee only for named Registry values and paths
open_points.default_guess: Make it an end-to-end platform guarantee and require every trusted service contract to prevent forwarding Registry personal data to Kernel or the agent.

open_points.subject: revision checks on owner changes
open_points.text: “Every change carries CSRF protection ... a change made against an older revision is refused” and “A project, a customer and an object carry a revision” are not reflected in archive, customer erasure, restriction, relationship, project erasure, grant, answer, active-project, revocation, import or audit-erasure actions, many of which name no revision input or stale-revision failure.
open_points.question: Which owner actions must present which revision or access version, and what happens when that version is stale, including nominally idempotent actions such as archiving an archived project or erasing an erased customer?
options: Every owner mutation requires a version of its affected aggregate
Only project, customer and object corrections require revisions
Project/customer mutations use record revisions; session mutations use access version; other actions use another declared concurrency rule
open_points.default_guess: Require the current project or customer revision for every mutation of that record, the access version for session mutations, and explicit operation-specific concurrency controls for import and audit erasure.

open_points.subject: session access concurrency
open_points.text: “read the session’s access” returns “the access version,” but grant, answer, change-active and revoke actions neither consume that version nor state when it changes.
open_points.question: What changes the access version, and must each owner mutation of session access supply the version it was based on?
options: All grant, revoke, active-project and request-answer changes increment and require it
It is output-only and mutations use last-write-wins
Only granted-set changes increment it
open_points.default_guess: Require and increment the access version for every mutation of the granted set, active project or pending-request outcome.

open_points.subject: audit event coverage
open_points.text: “entries of significant changes of state” and “Registry records only significant changes of state” do not settle whether session registration, access requests, active-project changes, artifact publication or withdrawal, migration, and refused mutation attempts produce audit entries.
open_points.question: Which exact actions and outcomes create audit entries, and are failed or refused attempts recorded when no state changed?
options: Audit every accepted state-changing primary action and no refusals
Audit only the events explicitly enumerated in R0-58
Audit accepted changes plus a declared set of refused security-sensitive attempts
open_points.default_guess: Audit every accepted state-changing primary action, including migration and session/access changes, and audit only explicitly designated security-sensitive refusals.
